title: Preparation of Botanical Extracts for In Vitro and In Planta Evaluation
author: Hemant Joshi
materials: Collect fresh plant materials such as ginger rhizome ( Zingiber officinale ), garlic cloves ( Allium sativum ), mugwort leaves ( Artemisia vulgaris ), and cinnamon leaves ( Cinnamomum verum ), used to extract active ingredients.
Clean the materials with distilled water to remove dust and debris.

Stock solutions are prepared based on the dry weight equivalent of plant material. About 1:1 w/v (fresh weight) for low moisture plant materials and 2:1 or 3:1 w/v for high moisture plant materials such as ginger rhizomes.

steps.title: Determine Botanical Moisture Content
steps.instruction: Calculate the dry matter content of each botanical sample using the oven-drying method to establish a conversion factor.

substeps.instruction: Weigh approximately 10–15 g of each fresh sample in four replicates.
Dry samples in a hot air oven at 105 °C for 16–18 hours.
Cool samples in a desiccator and record the dry weight.
Repeat drying, cooling, and weighing until a constant weight is obtained.
Calculate dry matter percentage using the formula: Dry matter (%) = (Wdw / Wfw) x 100, where Wdw is oven-dry weight (g) and Wfw is fresh weight (g).
Average the values across replicates to determine the conversion factor.

steps.title: Calculate Required Fresh Weight
steps.instruction: Determine the amount of fresh plant material needed to achieve the desired dry weight equivalent (w/v) concentration.

substeps.instruction: Use the formula: Wfresh = (C x V) / D, where Wfresh is required fresh weight (g), C is desired concentration (%), V is volume (mL), and D is dry matter percentage (%)
Example: To obtain 50 g dry matter per liter of water for a 5% solution, calculate the corresponding fresh weight.

steps.title: Homogenize Plant Material
steps.instruction: Process the calculated quantity of fresh plant material into a fine paste.

substeps.instruction: Clean the required quantity of fresh plant material.
Chop the material into small pieces.
Homogenize using an electric mixer grinder.

steps.title: Prepare Aqueous Extract
steps.instruction: Mix the homogenized material with distilled water to create a concentrated stock solution.

substeps.instruction: Add the appropriate volume of distilled water and mix thoroughly to achieve the desired concentration.
Allow the mixture to stand for approximately 1 hour at room temperature.

steps.title: Filter and Clarify Extract
steps.instruction: Remove plant debris and particulates from the mixture under sterile conditions.

substeps.instruction: Filter the mixture through four layers of muslin cloth.
Centrifuge the filtrate (e.g., 6,000 rpm for 10–15 min).
Collect the supernatant.
Pass the supernatant through a 0.22 μm membrane filter.

steps.title: Prepare Final Working Solution
steps.instruction: Dilute the stock solution and add a surfactant for application.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the stock solution to maintain a 5% concentration on a dry weight basis.
Add a wetting agent (e.g., Phytostick) to improve adherence to leaf and fruit surfaces.
Use the extracts within 6 hours of preparation to minimize degradation.
